title: Throughput Entropy Scrub — weekly perf sync (notes)
body:
Date: 2026-07-01
Meeting: Throughput Entropy Scrub — weekly perf sync
Organizer / note-taker: Maya Chen
Attendees: Maya Chen, Diego Alvarez, Priya Nair, Ethan Park, Lena Fischer, remote: Sam Ortega (SRE)
Objective: Rapidly capture and triage non-deterministic throughput regressions observed in last two shadow runs; produce a prioritized experiment list and owner assignments for next 7 days.

TL;DR:
- Recent shadow runs show intermittent 20–35% throughput drop under mixed short/long sequence mixes; p99 tail not always correlated with CPU/GPU utilization. We refer to these events as "entropy spikes" (temporary disorder in request dispatch/batching that causes inefficient packing).
- Two actionable hypotheses: 1) sampler-induced jitter + autoscaler probing causes fragmentation of batch formation windows, 2) KV-cache fragmentation after long prefix sequences increases per-request prep overhead.
- Immediate actions: run entropy-sweep A/B with controlled sampler jitter off (Priya, due 2026-07-03), run KV-cache defragmentation profile test (Diego, due 2026-07-04), and enable extra tracing for batch assembly timing across the dispatch boundary (Ethan + SRE, due 2026-07-02).

Observations and evidence captured:
- Shadow run IDs: shadow-2026-06-29-07, shadow-2026-06-30-03 (attached to Confluence link). Both runs used model variant: gpt-open-13b-quant-v2, seq distribution: mix 8/64/512 tokens, target qps=420.
- Run metrics: overall avg throughput drop observed ~22% during 3 separate 4-minute windows in shadow-2026-06-30-03. p95 increased from 85ms to 115ms, p99 from 180ms to 320ms in those windows. GPU util stayed ~74–81% (no shortage) and CPU for inference-agent spiked briefly but not enough to explain sustained throughput degradation.
- Trace pattern: batch assembly shows many small batches (size 1–3) appearing for several consecutive ticks instead of expected continuous 8–12 packing. The dispatcher logs show frequent short pauses (~12–50ms) coincident with autoscaler probe events.
- KV-cache telemetry: in the worst windows, per-request KV-restore time increased by ~30ms on average; the effect accumulates when a request sequence alternates between long prefix and short followups.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Sampler jitter + autoscaler probe overlap: the random jitter we inject to avoid thundering herd + aggressive autoscaler probes cause batch windows to fragment. When probe timing aligns with request arrivals, transient small batches form causing throughput loss.
2) KV-cache fragmentation: long prefixes populate cache shards unevenly; when short sequences arrive next, cache lookups require extra coordination (shard locking) increasing prep time. This shows up as KV-restore spikes.
3) Dispatcher backpressure mis-handled for mixed-request types: dispatcher sometimes falls back to immediate flush when mix is high, influenced by stale heuristics tuned for homogeneous workloads.
4) Model kernel path switching: for mixed sequence lengths the runtime occasionally triggers a suboptimal kernel path on the first chunk of long requests; subsequent tokens are fine. This would increase tail but not average GPU utilization.

Experiments and test plan (short-lived, measurable):
- Entropy-sweep A/B (Priya): run paired shadow runs with sampler jitter: default vs jitter disabled. Keep all other variables identical. Measure batch size distribution, throughput variance, and p99. Run window: 2 hours. Success criteria: if disable-jitter reduces entropy windows by >= 50% or reduces p99 by >20%, proceed to refine jitter windowing. Due: 2026-07-03.
- KV defrag profile (Diego): instrument KV-cache to emit per-shard lookup time and lock contention counters; run with synthetic workload that alternates long prefix sequences and short followups to reproduce fragmentation pattern. If lock contention > threshold, implement optimistic read path prototype. Due: 2026-07-04.
- Dispatcher flush-sensitivity tweak (Maya + Ethan): temporarily bump allowed assembly window by +10ms and change immediate flush threshold from N=1 to N=2 for mixed-traffic shadow runs. Goal: observe whether small-batch frequency decreases. Do not enable in production. Due: 2026-07-05.
- Kernel-path smoke (Lena): run trace-level capture on first 3 tokens for long sequences to detect kernel selection flips. Compare with control. If kernel flip correlates with latency spikes, open PR to add safe warmup path. Due: 2026-07-06.

Run configurations (note: provide exact knobs so tests are reproducible):
- Common: model=gpt-open-13b-quant-v2, sequence-mix=short:60%, med:30%, long:10%, target-qps=420, clients=120, seed=20260701
- Entropy-sweep-A: sampler.jitter=true, autoscaler.probe-interval=7s
- Entropy-sweep-B: sampler.jitter=false, autoscaler.probe-interval=7s
- KV-defrag-synth: alternating pattern: [long(512) x3, short(8) x50] repeat, client concurrency=80
- Dispatcher-tweak: assembly.window.ms=+10, flush.min_batch=2

Quick notes on instrumentation we need to add (Ethan action items):
- Batch assembly histogram (per-node) with 1ms bins for last 60s rolling window.
- Per-request KV-restore micro-timings (split by shard id).
- Autoscaler probe marker in trace (so we can correlate probe start/finish to batch windows).
- Add lightweight sampling for first-token kernel path selection events (for Lena's kernel smoke tests).

Action items (owner / due):
- Priya Nair: run Entropy-sweep A/B, gather batch-size distribution and p99 diff, publish results to Confluence. Due 2026-07-03.
- Diego Alvarez: KV defrag instrumentation and the synthetic repro; file notes and potential mitigation sketch. Due 2026-07-04.
- Ethan Park: add and roll a short-lived tracing build that includes autoscaler probe markers and batch assembly histogram. Coordinate with SRE for shadow runs. Due 2026-07-02.
- Lena Fischer: kernel-path smoke capture for first 3 tokens, summarize any path flips. Due 2026-07-06.
- Maya Chen: update playbook with "entropy windows" definition and quick triage checklist; schedule follow-up sync on 2026-07-07. Due 2026-07-05.

Risks and guardrails:
- Turning off sampler jitter in production is NOT recommended; A/B results will only guide heuristic adjustments (do not change production sampler behavior without rollout plan).
- Dispatcher assembly.window changes could increase latency for very low-concurrency customers; limit experiment to shadow/dedicated lanes with strict flags.
- KV instrumentation will add small CPU overhead; keep observability sampling rate low and limited to test nodes.

Parking lot / unresolved questions:
- Are autoscaler probes necessary at current aggressiveness? Could we reduce probe frequency or stagger probes across nodes? (SRE question: Sam Ortega to investigate fleet-wide probe policy, due 2026-07-08.)
- Could client-side batching knobs interact unexpectedly with server-side assembly heuristics? Need a small matrix test if initial experiments point to coordinator-level interaction.

Follow-up sync: 2026-07-07 09:00 PT (15m) — share A/B results and decide next rollback/rollforward actions.

Notes appended: quick pointer to related tickets and earlier runs: JIRA INF-2371 (throughput drift investigation), JIRA INF-2420 (kv-cache optimization spike), PR 4123 (dispatcher batching heuristics tweak prototype). Confluence doc for raw traces: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/cp/benchmark-entropy

End of notes.
